title: Sentence Structure
definition: German sentence structure describes where the subject, conjugated verb, and other sentence parts go. In a normal main clause, the conjugated verb is in position two; questions and commands follow different patterns.

rules.title: Basic statement
rules.explanation: A common pattern is subject + conjugated verb + other information.

rules.title: The conjugated verb is in position two
rules.explanation: Position two means the second sentence element, not always the second word. If time or place comes first, the subject usually comes after the verb.

rules.title: Time, manner, place
rules.explanation: A useful neutral order for several details is time, manner, place (TMP), although emphasis and context can change the order.

examples.german: Ich fahre morgen mit dem Bus nach Berlin.
examples.english: I am travelling to Berlin by bus tomorrow.
examples.note: Time: morgen; manner: mit dem Bus; destination/place: nach Berlin.

rules.title: Negation position
rules.explanation: Nicht often comes near the end when negating the whole action, but it can come before the specific word or phrase being negated.

examples.german: Ich fahre nicht mit dem Bus.
examples.english: I am not going by bus.

rules.title: Questions use different word order
rules.explanation: In a yes/no question, the conjugated verb comes first. In a W-question, the question word comes first and the verb follows.

common_mistakes.explanation: The conjugated verb stays in position two.
When a time phrase is first, the verb comes next and the subject follows.

mastery_goal: You can build simple statements and questions and keep the conjugated verb in the correct position.
